div.head: Cons Cn II 22.1b
div.ab: [Preiuramentum est unius hominis iurantis, antequam ille iuret qui Dei iudicium inire debet, et si contra illum qui ad Dei iudicium simplex uel ad Dei purgationem simplicem; triplex uero ad Dei iudicium uel purgatio attingi debet tribus preiurantibus.]
div.note: New row (October 2026): Liebermann’s text transcribed from Gesetze I p. 619 (two independent readings of the page images, differences settled against the page)

note.seg: 22, 1b aus Hk, verfasst vor Ordalabschaffung 1219, jedoch, wenn vom Verf., nur nachträglich, da Hr fehlend. Vgl. S. 418<sup>b</sup>
22, 1b from Hk, composed before the abolition of the ordeal in 1219, but, if by the author, only subsequently, since missing in Hr. Cf. p. 418<sup>b</sup>
Der Satz (z. T. aus II 22, 1a; vgl. 22, 2. 30, 3a) kann nach dem Wortschatz præiuramentum, attingere original sein, obwohl er sachlich 30, 3a widerspricht; s. Gl Klageeid 13d. e; Ordal 33

The sentence (partly from II 22, 1a; cf. 22, 2. 30, 3a) may be original, to judge by the vocabulary præiuramentum, attingere, although in substance it contradicts 30, 3a; see Gl Klageeid 13d. e; Ordal 33
